subject: maths
title: Circles and Nets: Radius, Diameter, 3-D Shapes and Nets
seo_title: Year 6 Circles and Nets Worksheets: Radius, Diameter, Faces, Edges, Vertices and Nets of 3-D Shapes (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Illustrate and name parts of circles, including radius, diameter and circumference and know that the diameter is twice the radius; recognise, describe and build simple 3-D shapes, including making nets; compare and classify geometric shapes based on their properties and sizes.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets on circles and nets: name the centre, radius, diameter and circumference, use diameter = 2 × radius, count faces, edges and vertices of 3-D shapes, and spot the nets of cubes, prisms and pyramids. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: The diameter is twice the radius: diameter = 2 × radius, and radius = diameter ÷ 2.
key_sub: A radius goes from the centre to the edge, a diameter goes across through the centre, and the circumference is the distance all the way round. A net is a flat shape that folds into a 3-D shape: each part becomes one face.
body_html:
Parts of a circle

Every point on the edge of a circle is the same distance from the centre.

  • The radius is a straight line from the centre to the edge.
  • The diameter is a straight line from edge to edge that passes through the centre.
  • The circumference is the distance all the way round the circle (its perimeter).

Diameter = 2 × radius

To find the diameter, double the radius. To find the radius, halve the diameter.

Example 1

A circle has a radius of 6.5 cm. What is its diameter?

Double the radius: 2 × 6.5 = 13.

Answer: 13 cm

Example 2

A circle fits exactly inside a square with sides of 14 cm. What is the radius of the circle?

The circle touches all 4 sides, so its diameter is 14 cm. Halve it: 14 ÷ 2 = 7.

Answer: 7 cm

3-D shapes: faces, edges and vertices

A face is a flat surface. An edge is where two faces meet. A vertex is a corner (two or more are vertices). Dashed lines show edges at the back that you cannot see.

ShapeFacesEdgesVertices
Cube6 (all squares)128
Cuboid6 (rectangles)128
Triangular prism5 (2 triangles, 3 rectangles)96
Square-based pyramid5 (1 square, 4 triangles)85
Tetrahedron4 (all triangles)64

Nets

A net is a flat shape that folds up to make a 3-D shape. Each part of the net becomes one face.

A cube has 11 different nets. A pattern of 6 squares is not a net if two squares would fold onto the same face.

Example 3

A net has 2 triangles and 3 rectangles. What 3-D shape does it make?

The 2 triangles are the ends and the 3 rectangles join them.

Answer: a triangular prism

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Halving the radius to get the diameterDiameter = 2 × radius; radius = diameter ÷ 2
Calling the circumference the diameterThe circumference goes all the way round; the diameter goes straight across
Calling any line across a circle a diameterA diameter must pass through the centre
Counting edges when asked for facesFaces are flat surfaces; edges are the lines where they meet
Forgetting the top vertex of a pyramidCount the base corners and the vertex at the top
Two squares on the same side of a row of 4 in a cube netPut one square on each side of the row

faq.q: What do Year 6 pupils learn about circles?
faq.a: They name the parts of a circle (centre, radius, diameter and circumference) and know that the diameter is twice the radius, so they can find one from the other.

faq.q: Do Year 6 children need to calculate the circumference?
faq.a: No. In Year 6 they only name the circumference. Working out the circumference and area of a circle with π is taught in Key Stage 3.

faq.q: How many nets does a cube have?
faq.a: A cube has 11 different nets. Each one has 6 squares, and no two squares fold onto the same face.

faq.q: Are circles and nets in the Year 6 SATs?
faq.a: They can be. Questions on the properties of shapes, such as radius and diameter or nets of 3-D shapes, can appear in the reasoning papers (Papers 2 and 3).

sets.title: Parts of a circle: centre, radius, diameter and circumference

items.q: What is the red line called?
items.e: It goes from one side of the circle to the other and passes through the centre, so it is a diameter.

items.q: The distance all the way round a circle is called the …
items.e: The circumference is the distance all the way round the edge of the circle. It is the perimeter of the circle.

items.q: Which point is the same distance from every point on the circumference of a circle?
items.e: Only the centre is the same distance from every point on the circumference. That distance is the radius.

items.q: A straight line from the centre of a circle to the circumference is called a …
items.e: A radius goes from the centre to the edge (the circumference). It is half of a diameter.

items.q: O is the centre of the circle. Which line is a radius?
items.e: OC goes from the centre O to the circumference, so it is a radius. AB is a diameter, and AC and BC do not start at the centre.

items.q: O is the centre of the circle. Which line is a diameter?
items.e: AB goes from one side of the circle to the other and passes through the centre O. AC and BC do not pass through O, and OC is a radius.

items.q: Which part of the circle is shown in red?
items.e: It goes from one side of the circle to the other and passes through the centre, so it is a diameter.

items.q: Which sentence about a circle is true?
c: The diameter is half the radius.
The radius is twice the diameter.
The diameter is twice the radius.
The radius and the diameter are equal.
items.e: A diameter is made of two radii in a straight line through the centre, so diameter = 2 × radius.

items.q: Which picture shows a diameter in red?
items.e: Picture B shows a diameter: it goes from edge to edge through the centre. The others are a radius, a line that misses the centre, and a line that stops before the edge.

items.q: The edge of this circle is shown in red. What is it called?
items.e: The circumference is the distance all the way round the edge of the circle. It is the perimeter of the circle.

items.q: The red line is part of this circle. What is it called?
items.e: It goes from the centre to the edge of the circle, so it is a radius. A diameter goes all the way across through the centre.

items.q: The red line is part of this circle. What is it called?
items.e: It goes from one side of the circle to the other and passes through the centre, so it is a diameter.

items.q: What is the longest straight line that can be drawn inside a circle, from edge to edge?
c: a line close to the edge
items.e: The longest line across a circle passes through the centre: that is a diameter. A radius is only half as long.

items.q: Which picture shows a radius in red?
items.e: Picture A shows a radius: it goes from the centre exactly to the circumference. The others are a diameter, a line that stops before the edge, and a line that goes past the edge.

items.q: What is the red line called?
items.e: It goes from the centre to the edge of the circle, so it is a radius. A diameter goes all the way across through the centre.

items.q: What is the red part of this circle called?
items.e: The circumference is the distance all the way round the edge of the circle. It is the perimeter of the circle.

items.q: Which part of the circle is shown in red?
items.e: It goes from the centre to the edge of the circle, so it is a radius. A diameter goes all the way across through the centre.

items.q: What is the red point called?
items.e: The centre is the point in the middle. Every point on the circumference is the same distance from the centre.

items.q: Ruby draws 5 different radii in the same circle. What is true about them?
c: The longest one is a diameter.
They are all the same length.
items.e: Every radius goes from the centre to the circumference, and every point on the circumference is the same distance from the centre.

items.q: A straight line from one side of a circle to the other that passes through the centre is called a …
items.e: It goes from one side of the circle to the other and passes through the centre, so it is a diameter.

sets.title: Radius and diameter: the diameter is twice the radius

items.q: A circle has a radius of 3 cm. What is its diameter in millimetres?
items.e: Diameter = 2 × 3 = 6 cm. 1 cm = 10 mm, so 6 cm = 60 mm.

items.q: The diameter of this circle is 3 m. What is the radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5 m.

items.q: The radius of this circle is 2.5 cm. What is the diameter?
items.e: The diameter is twice the radius: 2 × 2.5 = 5 cm.

items.q: The radius of this circle is 7 cm. What is the diameter?
items.e: The diameter is twice the radius: 2 × 7 = 14 cm.

items.q: A circle with a radius of 3 cm fits exactly inside a square. What is the perimeter of the square?
items.e: Each side of the square equals the diameter: 2 × 3 = 6 cm. Perimeter = 4 × 6 = 24 cm.

items.q: A circle has a diameter of 9 cm. What is its radius in millimetres?
items.e: 9 cm = 90 mm. The radius is half the diameter: 90 ÷ 2 = 45 mm.

items.q: Two equal circles fit exactly inside the rectangle. Each circle has a radius of 4 cm. How long is the rectangle?
items.e: Each circle is 2 × 4 = 8 cm across. Two diameters: 8 + 8 = 16 cm.

items.q: The radius of this circle is 4 cm. What is the diameter?
items.e: The diameter is twice the radius: 2 × 4 = 8 cm.

items.q: The radius of this circle is 15 m. What is the diameter?
items.e: The diameter is twice the radius: 2 × 15 = 30 m.

items.q: The diameter of this circle is 9 cm. What is the radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: 9 ÷ 2 = 4.5 cm.

items.q: The diameter of this circle is 26 mm. What is the radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: 26 ÷ 2 = 13 mm.

items.q: The circle has a radius of 6 cm and fits exactly inside the square. How long is each side of the square?
items.e: The side of the square is the same as the diameter of the circle: 2 × 6 = 12 cm.

items.q: Three equal circles fit exactly inside a rectangle 30 cm long. What is the radius of each circle?
items.e: The 3 diameters make 30 cm, so one diameter is 30 ÷ 3 = 10 cm. Radius = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm.

items.q: Circle A has a radius of 7 cm. Circle B has a diameter of 12 cm. Which circle is wider, and by how much?
items.e: Compare diameters: A is 2 × 7 = 14 cm across and B is 12 cm across. 14 − 12 = 2 cm, so A is wider by 2 cm. Do not compare a radius with a diameter (7 with 12), and do not stop at the radii (7 − 6 = 1).

items.q: Which of these is true for every circle?
items.e: Two radii in a straight line through the centre make a diameter, so diameter = 2 × radius and radius = diameter ÷ 2.

items.q: The diameter of this circle is 18 cm. What is the radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: 18 ÷ 2 = 9 cm.

items.q: A big circle has a radius of 12 cm. A small circle has a diameter that is the same length as the big circle’s radius. What is the radius of the small circle?
items.e: The small circle’s diameter is 12 cm, so its radius is 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm.

items.q: The radius of this circle is 12 mm. What is the diameter?
items.e: The diameter is twice the radius: 2 × 12 = 24 mm.

items.q: The circle fits exactly inside a square with sides of 10 cm. What is the radius of the circle?
items.e: The circle touches all 4 sides, so its diameter is the same as the side of the square: 10 cm. Radius = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm.

items.q: The diameter of this circle is 10 cm. What is the radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners. Dashed lines show the edges you cannot see.

items.q: Name this 3-D shape.
items.e: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism.
It has 2 flat circular faces and a curved surface, so it is a cylinder. A circle is a 2-D shape.

items.q: What shape are the faces of a cuboid?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces (some of them can be squares, which are special rectangles).

items.q: What is the name of this 3-D shape?
items.e: It has 4 faces and all of them are triangles, so it is a tetrahedron (a triangular-based pyramid).

items.q: How many edges does a cuboid have?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners.

items.q: What is the name of this 3-D shape?
items.e: It has 6 rectangular faces, and they are not all squares, so it is a cuboid.

items.q: What is this 3-D shape called?
items.e: It has a square base and 4 triangle faces that meet at one vertex, so it is a square-based pyramid.

items.q: This is a tetrahedron. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A tetrahedron has 4 triangular faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners. Dashed lines show the edges you cannot see.

items.q: Which of these 3-D shapes has no vertices?
items.e: A sphere is round all over: it has no flat faces, no edges and no vertices (corners).

items.q: I am a 3-D shape with 6 faces. All of my faces are squares of the same size. What am I?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces that are all equal squares. A cuboid has rectangular faces.

items.q: Which 3-D shape has 4 faces, and all of them are triangles?
items.e: A tetrahedron has 4 triangular faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices. A square-based pyramid has a square face as well.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners. Dashed lines show the edges you cannot see.

items.q: How many vertices does a square-based pyramid have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners.

items.q: I have 5 faces: 1 square and 4 triangles. What am I?
items.e: 1 square base and 4 triangles that meet at the top make a square-based pyramid.

items.q: This is a hexagonal prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A hexagonal prism has 8 faces (2 hexagons and 6 rectangles), 18 edges and 12 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners. Dashed lines show the edges you cannot see.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners. Dashed lines show the edges you cannot see.

items.q: How many vertices does a triangular prism have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners.

items.q: How many edges does a tetrahedron have?
items.e: A tetrahedron has 4 triangular faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners.

items.q: What is this 3-D shape called?
items.e: The two end faces are hexagons (6 sides) joined by rectangles, so it is a hexagonal prism. A hexagon is a 2-D shape.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?
items.e: C is not a net of a cube: two squares are on the same side of the row of 4, so they fold onto the same face and one face is left open. The other three each fold into a cube.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face C?
items.e: Faces C and F are in a straight line with one square between them, so they fold onto opposite sides of the cube.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face D?
items.e: Faces D and E are in a straight line with one square between them, so they fold onto opposite sides of the cube.

items.q: Which net folds into a triangular prism?
items.e: D has 3 rectangles and 2 triangles, one triangle at each end. One wrong net has only 2 rectangles, one has both triangles at the same end, and one is a square-based pyramid.

items.q: This net is folded up. What shape does it make?
items.e: There are 6 squares that are all the same size. They fold into a cube.

items.q: Which 3-D shape does this net make?
items.e: There is 1 square (the base) and 4 triangles that meet at the top. They fold into a square-based pyramid.

items.q: Oliver folds a net of 6 rectangles into a cuboid. How many edges does the cuboid have?
items.e: A cuboid has 12 edges (and 6 faces and 8 vertices). 6 is the number of faces.

items.q: Which 3-D shape does this net make?
items.e: There are 6 squares that are all the same size. They fold into a cube.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?
items.e: D is not a net of a cube: 5 squares in a row wrap all the way round, so the first and last squares overlap. The other three each fold into a cube.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face B?
items.e: Fold the net: face C lands opposite face B. A face that touches B in the net (A, D) is next to it on the cube, never opposite.

items.q: Which 3-D shape does this net make?
items.e: There are 2 triangles (the ends) and 3 rectangles. They fold into a triangular prism.

items.q: Which of these IS a net of a cube?
items.e: D folds into a cube with no gaps or overlaps. In the others, two squares fold onto the same face (two squares on the same side of a row of 4, 5 squares in a row, or a 2-by-2 block).

items.q: This net is folded up. What shape does it make?
items.e: There are 2 triangles (the ends) and 3 rectangles. They fold into a triangular prism.

items.q: How many faces does a net of a square-based pyramid have?
items.e: 1 square base and 4 triangles: 1 + 4 = 5 faces.

items.q: This net is folded up. What shape does it make?
items.e: There are 4 triangles and nothing else. They fold into a tetrahedron (a triangular-based pyramid).

items.q: Which of these IS a net of a cube?
items.e: A folds into a cube with no gaps or overlaps. In the others, two squares fold onto the same face (two squares on the same side of a row of 4, 5 squares in a row, or a 2-by-2 block).

items.q: This net is folded up. What shape does it make?
items.e: There are 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs, and they are not all squares. They fold into a cuboid.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?
items.e: C is not a net of a cube: two squares are on the same side of the row of 4, so they fold onto the same face and one face is left open. The other three each fold into a cube.

items.q: Which 3-D shape does this net make?
items.e: There are 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs, and they are not all squares. They fold into a cuboid.

items.q: Which net folds into a square-based pyramid?
items.e: B has 1 square and 4 triangles, one on each side of the square. The net with only 3 triangles leaves one side open; the others make a triangular prism and a tetrahedron.

items.q: A regular polygon has 6 equal sides and 6 equal angles. What is it called?
items.e: A polygon with 6 sides is a hexagon. All sides and angles are equal, so it is a regular hexagon. A hexagonal prism is a 3-D shape.

items.q: Charlie makes a model of a square-based pyramid. He uses straws for the edges and balls of modelling clay for the vertices. What does he need?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 8 edges (4 round the base and 4 up to the top) and 5 vertices (4 at the base and 1 at the top).

items.q: Ava paints each face of a cuboid box a different colour. How many colours does she use?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 faces, so she needs 6 colours. 12 is the number of edges and 8 is the number of vertices.

items.q: Which sentence is true?
items.e: A rectangle has 4 right angles and opposite sides equal. A square has both, so every square is a rectangle, but not every rectangle is a square.

items.q: A class sorts 3-D shapes into prisms and pyramids. Which shape goes with the pyramids?
items.e: A pyramid has a base and triangle faces that meet at one vertex. A tetrahedron is a triangular-based pyramid. Cubes, cuboids and triangular prisms are prisms.

items.q: A round pond has a diameter of 8 m. A fountain stands at the centre. How far is the fountain from the edge of the pond?
items.e: From the centre to the edge is a radius: 8 ÷ 2 = 4 m.

items.q: A triangle has sides of 5 cm, 5 cm and 8 cm. What type of triangle is it?
items.e: Exactly 2 sides are equal (5 cm and 5 cm), so it is isosceles.

items.q: A cube model is made from straws, one straw for each edge. Each straw is 10 cm long. What is the total length of the straws?
items.e: A cube has 12 edges: 12 × 10 = 120 cm. 60 cm counts the faces (6) and 80 cm counts the vertices (8).

items.q: Which quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides?
items.e: A trapezium has exactly one pair of parallel sides. A parallelogram and a rhombus have two pairs; a kite has none.

items.q: This is a net of a dice. The numbers on opposite faces add up to 7. What number goes on the face marked ?
items.e: When the net is folded, the face marked ? is opposite the 4. So the missing number is 7 − 4 = 3.

items.q: Ethan lines up 6 round counters in a straight row, each one touching the next. Each counter has a radius of 1.5 cm. How long is the row?
items.e: Each counter is 2 × 1.5 = 3 cm across. 6 counters: 6 × 3 = 18 cm. 9 cm uses the radius, and 15 cm counts only 5 counters.

items.q: The wheel on Amelia’s bike has a diameter of 60 cm. A spoke goes from the centre of the wheel to the rim. How long is a spoke?
items.e: A spoke goes from the centre to the edge, so it is a radius: 60 ÷ 2 = 30 cm.

items.q: Aisha uses a pair of compasses to draw a circle with a diameter of 9 cm. How wide should she open the compasses?
items.e: Compasses are opened to the radius: 9 ÷ 2 = 4.5 cm.

items.q: Alfie glues 2 cubes together, face to face, to make a cuboid. How many faces does the cuboid have?
items.e: The new shape is a cuboid, and every cuboid has 6 faces. The two faces that are glued together are hidden inside.

items.q: A tent is shaped like a triangular prism, with a groundsheet as the floor. How many faces does the tent have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces: 2 triangle ends and 3 rectangles (the 2 sloping sides and the floor).

items.q: The minute hand of a clock goes from the centre of the clock face exactly to its edge. The clock face has a diameter of 30 cm. How long is the minute hand?
items.e: From the centre to the edge is a radius: 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm.

items.q: A target is a small circle with a radius of 4 cm and 2 rings around it. Each ring is 4 cm wide. What is the diameter of the whole target?
items.e: The radius of the whole target is 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 cm, so the diameter is 2 × 12 = 24 cm. 16 cm forgets that the rings are on both sides of the centre.

items.q: A pizza has a diameter of 30 cm. It is cut into 8 equal slices with every cut passing through the centre. How long is each straight edge of a slice?
items.e: Each straight edge goes from the centre to the crust, so it is a radius: 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm. The number of slices does not change it.

items.q: I am a quadrilateral with 4 equal sides and no right angles. What am I?
items.e: 4 equal sides could be a square or a rhombus. A square has 4 right angles, so the shape is a rhombus.

items.q: Four tins of beans stand in a row in a box, touching each other and the ends of the box. Each tin has a radius of 5 cm. How long is the box?
items.e: Each tin is 2 × 5 = 10 cm across. 4 tins: 4 × 10 = 40 cm. 20 cm uses the radius instead of the diameter.
